mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding three months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by > 0.75% q/q over last 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a rise in unemployment (UNRATE) above 6% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of at least 100,000 for three consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises by > 100000 for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly above zero in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls > 0.5% m/m for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 3% signals a high-inflation, high-rate environment, which erodes real corporate earnings and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative in at least 60% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A consistent monthly decline in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) below 1 million units for six consecutive months signals a housing market contraction, which negatively impacts construction-related sectors and drags on overall equity returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative in at least 50% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 7% within a single month, accompanied by a decline in payroll employment (PAYEMS), signals a rapid labor market deterioration, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annualized GDP growth rate (GDPC1) below 1% for two consecutive quarters signals economic stagnation, which suppresses earnings growth and equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative in at least 50% of triggered episodes.
